name: Question 20
problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the straight line that passes through $P(9,3,-7)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨4,-5,3⟩.$
worked_solution:
Remember that the Cartesian (canonical) equation of the straight line that passes through the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=⟨{v}_{x},{v}_{y},{v}_{z}⟩$, is given by

$$
\frac{x-{x}_{0}}{{v}_{x}}=\frac{y-{y}_{0}}{{v}_{y}}=\frac{z-{z}_{0}}{{v}_{z}}=t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

So, we have

$$
\frac{x-9}{4}=\frac{y-3}{-5}=\frac{z-(-7)}{3}=t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty )
$$

or equivalently

$$
\frac{x-9}{4}=\frac{y-3}{-5}=\frac{z+7}{3}.
$$

Question 20
?

Find a Cartesian equation of the straight line that passes through P(9,3,−7) and is parallel to v=⟨4,−5,3⟩.

a
x−94=y−3−5=z+73
b
x+94=y+3−5=z−73
c
x4=y−5=z3
d
x+49=y−53=z+3−7
e
x−49=y+53=z−3−7
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Remember that the Cartesian (canonical) equation of the straight line that passes through the point P(x0,y0,z0) and is parallel to the vector v=⟨vx,vy,vz⟩, is given by x−x0vx=y−y0vy=z−z0vz=t,t∈(−∞,∞).

So, we have x−94=y−3−5=z−(−7)3=t,t∈(−∞,∞) or equivalently x−94=y−3−5=z+73.
